notes.heading: 3. de Broglie Matter Waves & Solar Photovoltaic Cell
notes.proseLatex: Every moving particle of momentum $p$ has de Broglie wavelength $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$; for an electron accelerated from rest across $V$ volts, $\lambda(\text{\AA}) \approx \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}$. A solar PV cell is an unbiased $p$-$n$ photodiode operating in the FOURTH quadrant of its $I$-$V$ plot (photovoltaic mode, no external bias!), absorbing $h\nu > E_g$ photons ($\text{Si}: E_g \approx 1.1\text{ eV},\; \text{GaAs} \approx 1.43\text{ eV}$) to sweep electron-hole pairs across the depletion field, characterized by $V_{\text{oc}}$, $I_{\text{sc}}$, and fill factor.

keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute matter-wave wavelengths and recall solar-cell fourth-quadrant operation.

wbjeebTraps:
Doubling light intensity NEVER doubles $K_{\max}$ or $V_s$ — it doubles saturation photocurrent (provided $
u > 
u_0$); if $
u < 
u_0$, current stays ZERO at any intensity!
Non-linear trap: doubling incident photon frequency ($2\nu$) makes $K_{\max}' = 2h\nu - \phi_0 = 2K_{\max} + \phi_0$, which is STRICTLY MORE than $2K_{\max}$!
Slope of $V_s$ vs $\nu$ is $h/e$, whereas slope of $K_{\max}$ vs $\nu$ is $h$ — check which axis is plotted!
